name: Bell Semiconductor
old_description: Bell Semiconductor is the successor in interest to the intellectual property portfolio that originated at Bell Labs following the invention of the transistor.  Semiconductor-related R&D continued as Bell Labs became part of Lucent Technologies, and then subsequently continues as a core competency of successor companies: Agere Systems, LSI, Avago and Broadcom.
about:
Bell Semiconductor is based in Chicago, Illinois. The company traces its lineage to the intellectual property portfolio that originated at Bell Labs following the invention of the transistor. That portfolio passed through Lucent Technologies, Agere Systems, LSI, Avago, and Broadcom before becoming the foundation of Bell Semiconductor. Key leaders include Chad Hilyard and Sailesh Merchant, both of whom previously held leadership roles in the intellectual property businesses at Lucent, Agere Systems, and LSI.

Bell Semiconductor licenses a semiconductor intellectual property portfolio that covers technologies enabling continued integration of semiconductor devices. The portfolio is licensed to virtually all foundries and integrated device manufacturers, supporting production of smartphones, PCs, tablets, wearables, and IoT devices. The company does not manufacture physical products; its business centers on patent licensing and technology transfer.

Its customers span the semiconductor manufacturing industry, including foundries and integrated device manufacturers that produce chips for consumer electronics, mobile communications, and internet-of-things markets. Licensees include major players in the smartphone, PC, tablet, wearable, and IoT device sectors.

The company exists to maintain and monetize the historic Bell Labs transistor patent portfolio, ensuring that foundational semiconductor inventions remain available to the industry. Its leadership’s deep experience in IP management at Lucent, Agere, and LSI positions it to administer this portfolio across the global semiconductor supply chain.

about:
Bellisio Foods, Inc. operates from Jackson, Ohio, where it produces frozen meals for retail brands and contract-manufacturing partners. The company does not disclose its founding year or ownership structure, but its history traces back to early quality practices attributed to an individual named Jeno, who conducted taste tests that shaped its quality-assurance culture.

The company runs full-scale production facilities that handle component processing, manufacturing, cooling, freezing, warehousing, and storage, turning out more than two million meals each day. A dedicated culinary center supports product development, where food scientists and chefs create new recipes and custom formulations for both Bellisio's own brands and partner labels. Services span research and development, commercialization support, and contract manufacturing.

Bellisio serves the frozen-food sector, supplying retail grocery brands, foodservice channels, and private-label partners. Its customer base includes companies seeking custom frozen-meal formulations and large-scale production capacity, though specific client names are not public.

Bellisio emphasizes innovation and consistent quality, positioning its culinary center and integrated production-to-warehousing flow as key differentiators. The company states it is dedicated to being an expert in the commercialization and production of the highest-quality frozen meals possible, with a quality-assurance program that began with sensory evaluation and continues through every production step.

about:
Belmont Market has operated in Wakefield, Rhode Island since 1947. The business describes itself as family-owned, with the tagline "fresh from our family to yours" reflecting its multi-generational roots. No individual founders are named in the available information.

The market runs a full-service grocery operation that includes deli, floral, grocery, health and wellness, meat, prepared foods, produce, seafood, and sushi departments. In addition to retail sales, it offers event catering, gift basket assembly, an online shopping platform with home delivery across Washington County and Jamestown, and curbside pickup. The company also maintains a wholesale division and a vendor inquiry program for suppliers.

Its primary customer base is local consumers seeking everyday groceries, prepared meals, and specialty items such as sushi and gift baskets. The wholesale channel and vendor inquiry page indicate it also serves other businesses, including local producers and food-service accounts, though specific client names are not disclosed.

Belmont Market emphasizes its commitment to local sourcing, stating it "keeps a focus on local where we can" and works to make shopping local easy for customers. The family-owned heritage and chef-prepared meals are presented as core differentiators.

name: Benco Equipment
old_description: for automotive equipment, service and financing for your business.
about:
Benco Equipment, headquartered in Bismarck, North Dakota, has served automotive professionals and hobbyists since 1972. The company operates as a family‑owned, six‑location network across the Midwest and functions as a division of Automotive Parts Headquarters Inc. (APH), a third‑generation family‑owned aftermarket parts distributor founded in 1920 as National Bushing & Parts Company in Minneapolis. APH today supports nearly 300 Auto Value stores and employs over 1,800 people across nine states.

Benco sells, installs, inspects, repairs and finances a broad range of automotive service equipment. Its product lineup includes vehicle lifts (light, medium and heavy‑duty, in‑ground, scissor and mobile), air compressors (piston and rotary screw), tire changers and wheel balancers, A/C machines from Robinair and MAHLE, waste‑oil heaters, piping systems in aluminum, stainless steel, copper and galvanized steel, lubrication systems, paint booths, Tommy Gate hydraulic lifts and exhaust systems. Each of the six branches – in Bismarck and West Fargo, ND; Eau Claire, WI; Hopkins and St. Cloud, MN; and Sioux Falls, SD – stocks a deep inventory of lifts, parts and maintenance supplies, backed by factory‑trained technicians who handle installation, mobile repair and on‑site inspection.

The customer base spans independent repair shops, dealership service departments, tire retailers, heavy‑duty fleet operators and motorcycle/ATV specialists throughout the Upper Midwest. Benco also serves hobbyists and DIY enthusiasts through its public‑access locations, offering financing options and a finance calculator on its website.

The company emphasizes its regional scale – “we sell and service more equipment than anyone in the region” – and its commitment to compliance, with inspection specialists following the current ANSI/ALI ALOIM standard. Its differentiation rests on a combination of extensive local stock, manufacturer‑trained service teams, and the backing of APH’s nine‑state distribution network.

All services are performed in-house and include design for manufacturing (DFM), precision mold manufacturing, injection molding, and detailed quality reporting. The engineering team also provides prototype design, mechanical design, and product development support.

The company serves customers who need plastic components across a range of applications, offering a single point of contact from initial design consultation to final part delivery. Bend Molding and Prototype emphasizes direct communication, giving clients access to engineers and toolmakers throughout the project. The team aims to deliver most prototype components within three to five weeks from DFM consultation to first samples, positioning itself as a domestic supplier that prioritizes collaboration and speed.

name: Benfield Control Systems Inc.
old_description: LV and MV power distribution equipment, including switchgear up to 38kV class
about:
Benfield Electric Supply Co. Inc. was founded in 1951 in Mount Vernon, New York, and remains independently owned. The company began as a wholesale electrical distributor serving the New York metropolitan area.

Today Benfield operates across six divisions — electric supply, data communications, electric and elevator supply, control systems, lighting, and international — from two locations in Mount Vernon and White Plains. A fleet of 24 service trucks supports same-day pickup and next-day delivery across New York City and the Lower Hudson Valley. The company maintains a broad inventory of electrical distribution equipment, wire, cable, conduit, lighting, and control products from hundreds of manufacturers. In-house capabilities include UL508a-listed control panel fabrication, SCADA and power monitoring system design, PLC/HMI software development, value engineering, and pre-fabrication services, all backed by RCDD-certified data engineers and FOA-certified fiber optic technicians.

Benfield serves industrial enterprises, original equipment manufacturers, construction and engineering contractors, manufacturing firms, and healthcare institutions such as Weill Cornell Medical Center and Lutheran Medical Center. Its project portfolio spans electrical distribution, data communications, power systems, HVAC, elevator equipment, lighting, and renewable energy installations including solar, wind, and EV charging infrastructure. The international division supplies U.S. and foreign engineering and construction contractors worldwide.

The company credits its longevity to independent ownership that allows flexibility and a relationship-focused approach, as well as deep community ties through local hiring and charitable involvement. Recognition such as the Westchester 50 award underscores its economic contribution. Benfield emphasizes combined staff experience exceeding 400 years and a service model that integrates project management from design through delivery.

about:
Founded in 1982 in Paterson, New Jersey, Bennett Plastics is a family-owned and operated custom plastic injection molding company. Located just minutes from New York City, the business began as a local manufacturer and has grown to serve customers nationwide from its 36,000-square-foot facility.

The company provides a full range of in-house services including custom plastic injection molding, 3D printing and prototyping, product development and design for manufacturing, injection mold making, and finishing and packaging. Its Paterson facility produces millions of parts annually, supported by a team of experienced professionals across operations, engineering, quality, and production.

Bennett Plastics serves diverse industries such as baby products, food service, consumer goods, health and beauty, electrical, industrial products, and pharmaceutical. The company works with clients from initial concept through full-scale production, tailoring solutions to each sector's requirements.

The company differentiates itself by keeping all manufacturing on-site with no outsourcing, enabling direct communication, strict quality control, and fast delivery. Its Fast-Track Mold Insert Program can deliver molded samples in as little as five weeks. A zero-defects quality objective, adherence to OSHA and Good Manufacturing Practices, and a sustainability focus using eco-friendly materials and waste reduction further define its approach.

name: Benteler Automotive Corporation
old_description: Since the company was founded by Carl Benteler in 1876, foresight has been the foundation of our success. From trading to manufacturing, from a regional supplier to an international technology leader – BENTELER has always moved ahead while others hesitated.
about:
Benteler Automotive Corporation, headquartered in Goshen, Indiana, traces its roots to 1876 when Carl Benteler opened a small hardware store in Bielefeld, Germany. The family-founded enterprise evolved from trading into a global metal-processing specialist, now operating as a tier 1 automotive supplier with a presence in 25 countries.

The company manufactures chassis components, module assemblies, and precision steel tubes—both seamless and welded—along with free-cutting steel tubes that replace machined bar stock. Core processes include stamping, assembly, tube forming, and steel production, supported by tool shops and engineering hubs across roughly 90 locations worldwide. The group employs more than 20,000 people.

Benteler serves the automotive industry as a primary customer, supplying OEMs with structural and safety-critical parts, while its steel/tube division serves energy and industrial markets with high-load-capacity tubing for applications such as pipelines and machinery.

The company emphasizes pioneering spirit and sustainability, aiming to make mobility safer and more sustainable through integrated systems like its highly integrated crash management system and material innovations that reduce weight and coating steps.

name: Benton & Sons
old_description: Custom fabricated steel parts and components, structural steel fabrications, steel machine bases and more. Specializes in large component steel fabrication.
about:
Benton & Sons Fabrication operates from Pikeville, North Carolina, about 60 miles southeast of Raleigh. Founded in 1983 by the Benton family, the business remains family‑owned and operated, with three generations having worked in the shop. Owner Ben Benton Jr. now leads a company that has grown into one of the largest plate‑rolling, brake‑press‑forming, and machinery‑assembly facilities in the southeastern U.S.

The 100,000‑sq‑ft facility includes multiple bays, large overhead doors, and overhead cranes for oversized work. Core capabilities cover heavy steel plate fabrication, stainless steel sheet metal fabrication, plate rolling, brake‑press forming, laser cutting, water‑jet cutting, punching, shearing, welding, and custom machinery assembly. Key equipment includes a 1,000‑ton × 24‑ft CNC Cincinnati brake press, a TRUMPF 6,000‑watt TruLaser 5060, and a Mitsubishi 6030XL laser cutter — each noted as rare in the region. Output ranges from custom steel parts, structural fabrications, and machine bases to stainless enclosures, commercial kitchen equipment, pharmaceutical and lab equipment, and metal yard art.

Customers span the Southeast and Mid‑Atlantic, including Maryland, Virginia, the Carolinas, and Georgia. Served industries include food processing, commercial kitchens, pharmaceutical plants, shipbuilding, nuclear facilities, transportation, beverage bottling, and fine chemicals. Access to I‑95, I‑40, rail, and East Coast ports enables worldwide shipment of large assemblies.

The company stresses quick turnaround, on‑time/on‑budget delivery, and an experienced workforce. During the 2008‑2009 recession, ownership commissioned a large dinosaur sculpture to keep workers employed and hone fabrication skills, underscoring a commitment to workforce stability and continuous improvement.
